questions.question: In standard dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) architectures, why does reading data from a 1T-1C (one-transistor, one-capacitor) storage cell inherently require a write-back (restoration) operation?
options: The read operation transfers the capacitor's stored charge onto the bitline via charge sharing, disturbing the original stored voltage level.
The sense amplifier must invert the stored charge in order to register a logical '1', requiring a restore pulse to flip it back.
DRAM wordlines are driven by negative gate voltages that permanently drain the storage node during access.
The row decoder disables active precharge logic during read operations, forcing the memory cell into an unpowered high-impedance state.
The storage cell's access transistor undergoes channel hot-carrier degradation during every read cycle, requiring an electrical recharge cycle.

questions.question: In synchronous digital circuits, why can a setup timing violation be eliminated by lowering the clock frequency, whereas a hold timing violation cannot?
options: Hold timing checks are evaluated only during the power-up initialization phase, whereas setup checks run continuously during normal operation.
Hold constraints depend strictly on the difference between data path delay and clock skew, independent of the clock period, whereas the setup constraint explicitly includes the clock period.
Hold violations only occur when dynamic power dissipation exceeds thermal design limits, which is unaffected by clock frequency.
Setup time is determined by sequential standard cells, while hold time is determined purely by combinational routing delays that adaptively track clock rate.
Hold checks verify data arrival relative to the next subsequent clock edge, whereas setup checks verify arrival relative to the identical clock cycle edge.

questions.question: In high-performance microprocessor memory hierarchies, what is the primary microarchitectural purpose of Miss Status Holding Registers (MSHRs) in a non-blocking cache?
options: To store dirty cache lines evicted during a write-back before they are written to main memory, preventing pipeline stalls on evictions.
To perform speculative prefetching by calculating stride patterns across sequential misses.
To track in-flight outstanding cache misses and collate subsequent requests to the same cache block, enabling hit-under-miss and miss-under-miss execution.
To dynamically remap set-associative cache ways into direct-mapped banks when conflict misses exceed a runtime threshold.
To buffer tag comparisons during snooping operations to prevent coherency probes from stalling the L1 instruction cache.

questions.question: In high-performance digital VLSI arithmetic, what represents the primary architectural trade-off between a Kogge-Stone adder and a Brent-Kung adder of equal bit width?
options: Kogge-Stone operates strictly on two's complement numbers, while Brent-Kung is restricted to unsigned binary arithmetic due to tree symmetry.
Brent-Kung eliminates all lateral fan-out routing at the cost of requiring tri-state bus repeaters on all intermediate sum outputs.
Brent-Kung achieves lower power dissipation solely by using dynamic domino logic stages, whereas Kogge-Stone requires static CMOS transmission gates.

Kogge-Stone achieves minimal logic depth (O(log2 N)) with higher wiring density and cell area, whereas Brent-Kung minimizes area and routing density at the cost of higher logic depth (O(2 log2 N - 1)).
Kogge-Stone requires zero carry-generation cells at odd indices, whereas Brent-Kung requires lookahead generator cells at every bit position.

questions.question: In directory-based cache coherence protocols for scalable shared-memory multi-core architectures, what is the primary operational trade-off of implementing a 'limited pointer' directory scheme instead of a 'full bit-vector' directory scheme?
options: It eliminates the need for invalidation traffic by enforcing write-through caching at all private cache levels.
It simplifies router microarchitecture by guaranteeing single-flit point-to-point coherence message transmission across the on-chip network.
It converts cache coherence from an invalidation-based model to an update-based model whenever a pointer limit is reached.
It prevents protocol deadlocks by eliminating the need for request, response, and forward virtual networks in the on-chip fabric.

It substantially reduces directory memory overhead as core count scales, but incurs performance degradation or broadcast invalidations when the number of concurrent sharers exceeds the fixed pointer capacity.
